correctness.rationale: For normalized uniform solid measure and the degree-one orthogonal L2 projector, symmetry/second moments give K_D(x,y)=1+[(d+1)(d+2)/2] x·y on the cross-polytope and K_Q(x,y)=1+3x·y on the cube. For any x the L∞ row norm is E|K(x,Y)|; convexity in x forces a maximizing vertex, and a positive-volume region with opposite signs of K(v,y) and K(w,y) for distinct vertices makes convexity strict for any nonvertex. At a cross-polytope vertex, the one-coordinate beta density d(1−t)^{d−1} gives 1+(d+2)/2[1−2/((d+1)(d+2))]^{d+1}; the cube row is an Irwin–Hall truncated-power sum 1+12/(d+1)!Σ_{k≤floor((3d−1)/6)}(−1)^k binom(d,k)((3d−1)/6−k)^{d+1}. The signed kernel input attains the norm, while its negative part gives sharp positivity loss (norm−1)/2. Beta asymptotics yield normD/d→1/2; the CLT with uniform integrability gives normQ/√d→√(6/π), hence divergence of normD/normQ. Independent exact rational calculations in dimensions 1..9 reproduce all formula values and special cases d1=5/3,d2=233/108,d3=10561/4000 versus 415/162; small d checks do not prove asymptotic/strict vertex claims.
